findings.description: The promised reverse-layout dry-run integration case is missing. New tests call discovery helpers directly; existing dry-run tests create canonical filenames. They do not establish that reverse-layout discovery preserves root Verification ownership and avoids execution or evidence writes through the CLI.
findings.recommendation: Cover a reverse-only amendment through the CLI dry-run, with conflicting amendment-local Verification content and assertions that root rows remain authoritative and no execution or recording occurs.

findings.description: Containment and ambiguity checks inspect candidate paths before reopening them. A candidate replaced between resolve() and read_bytes(), or between discovery and read_text(), can bypass the checked containment or supply different declarations from the bytes compared. Static escaping symlinks are rejected, but concurrent replacement is not protected.
findings.recommendation: Read and validate a stable file handle, then parse those same validated bytes rather than reopening the candidate path.

findings.description: The supplied scope contains verification commands and test source, but no executed results tied to these inputs. Functional execution and security regression evidence remain incomplete. No tests were run during this review, as requested.
